items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:46:1
items.html:
Lo Mati in Keter, etc., and Mati in Hod, and Lo Mati in Yesod, for it rose into Hod; and then it turns its face and gives light to Malchut below in her place, and then it is Mati in Malchut: The matter of Lo Mati in Keter has already been explained: that it is by reason of the usual refinement through the clash of the inner light with the surrounding light, when phase three in the vessel refined to phase two, the light emerging in this coupling being the level of Bina; and this remainder Keter gave to the vessel of Hochma, and so forth, as above. And since the illumination of GAR returned to the Partzuf, all the aspects of the face of Hochma and Bina and Hesed and Tifferet and Hod returned to their place as at first. And then the light of Yesod is found to rise and join with the illumination of the face of GAR of Hod, for the above reason; and then the vessel of Yesod is found to turn its face downward, that is, that it too bestows the aspect of the illumination of GAR by virtue of the rule of the vessel of Hod over it — only not from phase one, but from the level of the light of Malchut, since the light that remained in the vessel of Yesod is only the level of Malchut, as above. And then it is Mati in Malchut.
However, one must know here what the light of Yesod is that rose to Hod, and what its remainder is that it gave to the vessel of Malchut. And one must know, with especial depth, the origin of the above Hey who descended to the vessel of Yesod. And you already know that this Hey is an offspring of the coupling of the ZON that are in the vessel of Bina. And one must further know that in the form of this Hey there is a Dalet upon a Vav, which is the Vav inside the Hey that has no head. And there is in this an important hint: for this Hey is included of the male and female of Bina, and therefore the aspect of the female in the Hey is the secret of the Dalet, and the aspect of the male in the Hey is the secret of the Vav without the head within her.
And the explanation of these words is this. The matter of the break in the left leg, in the secret of the Hey, indicates the severance of the GAR from the VAK that was prepared and made within the vessel of Bina. For you will see a great novelty: that the female is more important than her male. For the male is an offspring that comes from the coupling of the male and female of the vessel of Hochma at the time when the male is in the aspect of the bowing of the head, as above in the words of the ARI (page 316, item 35, and in the Inner Light there, the passage beginning “Hochma”), that Hochma turned her face and illuminates to Bina face to face, an illumination alone, etc. Its meaning is that the male that is in the vessel of Hochma, which is phase three, turned its face and refined to phase two, like the Nukva of the vessel of Hochma; and so the male is found to have bowed its head, for the GAR of Hochma is called head, since now, after it departed from the coarseness of phase three, the light of Hochma vanished from it entirely, and it becomes equal with the level of Bina of its female. And then they coupled and gave birth to the above male of the vessel of Bina. And it is known that every son and offspring is discerned as the aspect of the VAK of its emanator; thus the degree of the male is the aspect of the VAK of the level of Bina alone, for his emanator — that is, the male and female of Hochma, who gave birth to him — had at the time they gave birth to him nothing but the level of Bina alone, as above, and so their son is only the VAK of this level, as above.
However, the female of the vessel of Bina is the aspect of the record of Bina that remained in that vessel from the time of the first expansion, which the light of Bina of the first expansion left there at the time of her departure from there. And this light of Bina had there the level of Keter, for all the ten Sefirot of the first expansion had the level of Keter, as is known. And you see the great importance of this record that remained in the vessel of Bina. And even so she became a Nukva to the male of the vessel of Bina, who lacks even the GAR of Bina, as above. And this was for the reason that this record has very little light, for all her light has already departed and she is only a record, which means a very small light that must remain after every light at the time when it departs from the place in which it was. And therefore, since the record lacks light, she became the aspect of a female to the above light of the male, which is much lower than she, in order to receive light from him. And understand this.
Now you will thoroughly understand the secret of the above Hey, who was emanated from these male and female. For the truncated Vav, without a head, that stands inside the Hey is the aspect of the male in this offspring, since he is the aspect of the VAK of the level of Bina and lacks the aspect of the head of the level of Bina, as above; and therefore the Vav that is drawn from him is likewise truncated, without a head. And the Dalet that encompasses this truncated Vav that is in the Hey is the aspect of the female in this offspring, and she is discerned as a head upon the truncated Vav, being entirely the aspect of GAR, as above — except that she lacks light, which the truncated Vav has, so that her whole light is only what she receives from this truncated Vav. And therefore she is called by the name Dalet, to indicate that she is “Dala” [poor] and empty of abundance from her own aspect, and must receive from her male.
And the secret of the break made in the left leg of the Hey indicates that she was severed into two degrees separate from one another; and this is what is now done through the ascent of the light of Yesod to the Sefira of Hod, as above. For you know the two kinds of lights that are in the vessel of Yesod. The first is the aspect of the judgments that remained in Hod after the illumination of GAR vanished there, as above. And the second is the light of the Hey that was drawn to it from the ZON that are in Bina, as above. And after Mati of the light in Hod — which is the aspect of the illumination of GAR that had been separated from the light of Yesod at the time when that light was in Hod, for which reason its remainder descended to Yesod — it now turns out that when that light again descended to Hod, the remainder that had descended to Yesod certainly returned to its root, to Hod, which now has there its own illumination of GAR once more. And this light, at the time when it rose, took with it also the aspect of the truncated Vav that is inside the Hey in Yesod, and raised it to Hod. So that two lights rose from Yesod: the first is the above light of Malchut, that is, the remainder that it had earlier taken from Hod; and the second is the truncated Vav that is inside the Hey. And the reason for this is that although that Vav is not at all of the aspect of Hod, it nevertheless rose there; and this is because it had earlier been joined to the light of Malchut in order to sweeten her, as above — for the light of Malchut is the aspect of the five Gevurot and the Hey is the aspect of the five Hassadim, and they were sweetened one in the other, study it there. And this sweetening came only from the Vav that is inside the Hey, since it is the whole of the light inside the Hey; yet it certainly also took from the Dalet the illumination of GAR that is in her — that is, only during the time of Lo Mati in Hod, when it was in Yesod without the illumination of GAR. But now that the illumination of GAR is Mati again in Hod, it no longer needs the illumination of GAR that is in the aspect of the Dalet; and therefore, when it rose there, it took only the aspect of the Vav and not the aspect of the Dalet that encompasses it. And know that that aspect of the Dalet that encompasses it descended and clothed in the vessel of Malchut.
And now the Sefira of Malchut is thoroughly understood, for the vessel in her is a vessel of Malchut that was drawn from the vessel of Hod, as above; and the light in her is the aspect of the Dalet that encompasses the Vav, of the aspect of the Hey that is drawn from the ZON of Bina, as above. However, the light of Malchut herself is what clothed here in the vessel of Yesod, as above. And therefore Malchut is called a mirror that does not illuminate, as the ARI says above in Part 4, study it there.
And you find that there are four males and four females in this second expansion. The first two pairs are the ZON of Keter and the ZON of Hochma. And in them the males are more important than the females, for the male of Keter is of phase four of clothing whereas the female of Keter is only of phase three, and the male of the vessel of Hochma is of phase three whereas the female of the vessel of Hochma is of phase two; thus the males are greater than the females. But even so, in both pairs the males and females are found in a single vessel, since they have a closeness to one another, because the males are of the records that remained after the departure of the first expansion and are therefore lacking in light, whereas the females are of the new second expansion and are full of light.
But in the male and female of the vessel of Bina, the female is found to be greater than the male, for the male is the aspect of the VAK of Bina and the female is the aspect of the GAR of Bina. And even so both of them are in a single vessel, because the female is of the record and lacks light, whereas the male comes from the coupling of the ZON of Hochma and is therefore full of light. And likewise the male that is in the vessel of Keter: although he is a record, which is discerned as lacking light, this lack is said only with regard to his GAR, whereas he is full of light in the aspect of VAK.
However, in the male and female of the VAK there are many discernments. For the male, who is the light of ZA, was emanated through Hochma, being the light of Hesed that was in the vessel of Bina and afterwards expanded to the vessel of ZA, as above. But the female is an offspring of Bina, that is, the Hey who was emanated through the ZON of Bina.
However, there is a further aspect of male and female to be discerned there, namely the male and female that are in Yesod and Malchut; and there the male is smaller than the female, for the male is the aspect of the Vav without a head that is inside the Hey, drawn from the male of Bina, who is the aspect of VAK, as above. And even so they are not in a single vessel: rather the male is in the upper vessel, which is Yesod, and the female is in the lower vessel, which is Malchut.
And these two aspects of ZON that are within the seven lower Sefirot are reckoned sometimes as one and sometimes as two. For in Gadlut the female has the whole of the above Hey, and all the VAK are then reckoned as the male of this Hey; but in Katnut only Yesod is reckoned as the aspect of the male, and Malchut then has only the Dalet that is in the Hey, for Yesod takes the truncated Vav. And in this too there are many variations, and this is not the place to elaborate.
One must further discern here that there are three divisions in the seven lower ones, which are the aspect of Rosh, Toch and Sof. The first are Hesed and Gevura, and they are the aspect of the Rosh of the VAK. The second are Tifferet and Netzah, and they are the aspect of the Toch of the VAK. The third are Hod, Yesod and Malchut, and they are the aspect of the Sof of the VAK. And the matter of Mati and Lo Mati depends only on Keter and Hochma, and this is because the posterior of Keter withholds the illumination of GAR from the whole Partzuf; and therefore it is impossible for there to be an illumination of GAR in the Partzuf except by the annulment of the rule of Keter, namely through the refinement of the coarseness in the screen in it that belongs to its level. And then the light departs from Keter, and its remainder is Mati in Hochma, from which the illumination of GAR appears in the Partzuf.
And therefore, if it is Mati in Keter, every illumination of GAR is withheld even from Hochma; and therefore the aspect of the VAK of the seven lower Sefirot then rules — that is, the VAK of the Rosh among them, which is the Sefira of Gevura; and the VAK of the Toch among them, which is Netzah; and the VAK of the aspect of the Sof among them, which is Yesod.
And if it is Lo Mati in Keter, so that it is Mati in Hochma, then the rule of the illumination of GAR reaches the RTS [Rosh-Toch-Sof] of the seven lower Sefirot, that is: the aspect of the illumination of GAR of their Rosh, which is Hesed; and the aspect of the illumination of GAR of their Toch, which is Tifferet; and the aspect of the illumination of GAR of their Sof, which is Hod — from which the aspect of GAR without VAK reaches Malchut, which is called the Dalet that is upon the Vav, found in the form of the letter Hey.
And the matter of this Dalet means the cessation of the light from the Partzuf. For all the coarseness in the screen refined and the coupling ceased, and there is no longer any reflected light there to clothe the direct light, and the direct light, too, ceased, and all the Sefirot return to the Emanator — that is, through the inclusion of all the records in them within the screen, for only the screen rises to the Emanator, as written in Part 4 in the Inner Observation, study it there.

items.html: And now the first aspect, which is the existence of the expansion, has been completed. That is, the existence of the second expansion, which is called the Partzuf AB of AK.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:46:3
items.html:
And behold, all ten lights have reached down to Malchut. That is, that the refinement has reached the level of Malchut, when the screen is found clean of all the coarseness of the aspect of the Guf, until its form is equal to the aspect of the screen of the Malchut of the Rosh — and this is what is discerned as its having risen there and been included in the coupling that never ceases in the Malchut of the Rosh. And then the records of the Sefirot of the Guf that are included in it return and awaken, in all the measure of their coarseness, and it thickens once more in the coarseness of the aspect of the Guf; and thereby its form has again changed from the Malchut of the Rosh, and it is therefore discerned as emerging from there and becoming separate on its own. And then an upper coupling emerges upon it, and it draws a new level of ten Sefirot to the Guf, as written in Part 4, study it there.
And it was explained there that the last phase leaves no record. And since the last phase here was phase three, phase three left no record and is therefore not included in the screen, and the greatest record in it is phase two. And therefore, when the screen returned and thickened out of its inclusion in the coupling of the Rosh, it could not thicken further than to phase two; and so the level that emerged there reached only the level of Bina, as is known. And this is the second aspect of the expansion of the light, after its departure a second time.
